entries.title: Nehemiah 1:1
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: Book Introduction - Nehemiah Read first chapter of Nehemiah Fourteen years after the return of Ezra to Jerusalem, Nehemiah led up a company (B.C. 444) and restored the walls and the civil authority. Of those events this book is the record. It is in eight divisions: The journey to Jerusalem, 1:1-2:20 The building of the wall, 3:1-6:19. The census, 7:1-73. The revival, 8:1-11:36. The census of the priests and Levites, 12:1-26. Dedication of the wall, 12:27-43. Restoration of the temple worship, 12:44-47. The legal order restored, 13:1-31. The moral state of the time is disclosed by the prophet Malachi. This book affords many instances of individual faith acting on the written word (e.g. Nehemiah 1:8,9; 13:1). It is the principle of 2 Timothy 2. The events recorded in Nehemiah cover a period of 11 years (Ussher). SCOFIELD REFERENCE NOTES (Old Scofield 1917 Edition) The Book of Nehemiah Fourteen years after the return of Ezra to Jerusalem, Nehemiah led up a company (B.C. 444) and restored the walls and the civil authority. Of those events this book is the record. It is in eight divisions: I. The journey to Jerusalem, 1:1-2:20; II. The building of the wall, 3:1-6:19. III. The census, 7:1-73. IV. The revival, 8:1-11:36. V. The census of the priests and Levites, 12:1-26. VI. Dedication of the wall, 12:27-43. VII. Restoration of the temple worship, 12:44-47. VIII. The legal order restored, 13:1-31. The moral state of the time is disclosed by the prophet Malachi. This book affords many instances of individual faith acting on the written word (e.g. Nehemiah 1:8,9; 13:1). It is the principle of 2Ti 2. The events recorded in Nehemiah cover a period of 11 years (Ussher). Chisleu i.e. December. Shushan Or, Susa, ancient capital of Persia.

entries.title: Nehemiah 2:10
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: Tobiah Two Tobiahs are distinguished by many: (1) "Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite," Nehemiah 2:10,19; 4:3,7 6:1,12,14. (2) A Jew, unable to prove his genealogy. But the reference to the latter (Nehemiah 7:62) indicates that he was already dead. But one Tobiah, and he the Ammonite, is active in this book.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:1
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: sheep The sheep for sacrifice were brought in here. (See Scofield "John 5:2") . tower The towers appear to have been on either side the sheep gate.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:26
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: Nethinims i.e. dedicated (persons), probably descendants of the Gibeonites 2 Samuel 21:1-3 devoted to the service of the Levites. But see Joshua 9:17-21.

entries.title: Nehemiah 3:27
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: Ophel Trans. "tower," 2 Kings 5:24; 2 Chronicles 27:3; 33:14. Perhaps part of the fort called Millo, ; 1 Kings 9:15; 2 Chronicles 32:5.

entries.title: Nehemiah 8:17
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: for since the days of Jeshua It is not meant that there had not been some formal observance of the feast of tabernacles (cf) 2 Chronicles 8:13; Ezekiel 3:4, but that the people had not dwelt in booths since Joshua's days.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:14
entries.author: C. I. Scofield (1843–1921)
entries.content: madest known unto them This important passage fixes beyond all cavil the time when the sabbath, God's rest Genesis 2:1-3 was given to man. Cf. Exodus 20:9-11. In Exodus 31:13-17 the sabbath is invested with the character of a sign between Jehovah and Israel. (See Scofield "Matthew 12:1") .
